question.leadin: This place was originally known as the Flavian Amphitheatre.
question.text: Name this structure which included 80 entrances. Its construction began under the emperor Vespasian [veh-SPAY-zhun] and was completed under the emperor Titus.
question.clue: The construction of a complex tunnel network at this structure, its hypogeum ("hy-PO-jee-um"), ended the prior practice of flooding this place for mock naval battles.

swap.leadin: A period of expansion into Germany under this ruler was ended by defeat at the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.
swap.text: Name this first Emperor of Rome, who conquered Egypt through victory at the Battle of Actium.
swap.answerHtml: Octavian [or Augustus Caesar or Gaius Octavius; do not accept or prompt on just “Caesar”]
swap.clue: The Second Triumvirate consisted of Antony, Lepidus, and this adopted son of Julius Caesar, who fought a civil war against Antony and Cleopatra in 31 BCE and became the first Emperor of Rome.

question.leadin: This man's mother, Agrippina, killed the emperor Claudius, before this man killed her.
question.text: Name this crazy Roman emperor who supposedly "fiddled while Rome burned" and persecuted early Christians.
question.answerHtml: Nero Claudius Caesar Augustus Germanicus [or Nero Claudius Caesar Drusus Germanicus; or Lucius Domitius Ahenobarbus]
question.clue: He was closely advised by his mother Agrippina and a writer who allegedly participated in the Pisonian Plot against this figure, Seneca the Younger.

swap.text: This Roman farmer and statesman inspired the Third Punic War and sacking of Carthage by ending all of his speeches "Carthago delenda est," or "Carthage must be destroyed!"
swap.clue: During a particularly brutal campaign in part of Hispania, this man apocryphally declared "the war feeds itself."

question.text: The First and Second Servile Wars were fought in Sicily, but the Third Servile War ended when this Thracian man was killed in battle and six thousand former slaves were crucified along the Appian Way.
question.clue: After Crassus defeated this man, Pompey arrived from Spain and took credit for the victory.

swap.text: This man commanded the cavalry at the Battle of Alesia. Later, this man was a member of the Second Triumvirate with Octavian and Marcus Lepidus before commmitting suicide after the Battle of Actium.
swap.clue: This man was criticized by Cicero's Philippics and delivered the eulogy at Julius Caesar's funeral.

question.text: Lars Porcena was ostensibly helping this man regain his control of Rome. This man, supposedly the son of an earlier king with a similar name, lost power after his son raped Lucretia.
question.answerHtml: Tarquin the Proud [accept Lucius Tarquinius Superbus; prompt on Tarquinius; do not accept "Lucius Tarquinius Priscus]
question.clue: This last king of Rome was legendarily deposed and exiled after his son Sextus raped Lucretia, the wife of Lucius Collatinus.

swap.leadin: Caracalla is presented by many sources as a tyrant, but he wasn't all bad.
swap.text: One of Caracalla's great public projects was the construction of his namesake one of the these things, the second-largest in Rome. These places were fed water by aqueducts which was then heated by log fires.
swap.clue: Slaves called unctores would often use a strigil on their masters in the destrictarium of these places.

question.leadin: As part of the Second Triumvirate, Lepidus received this office.
question.text: Name this chief priest of the Roman religion.
question.clue: Per the Lex Ogulnia, the plebeian Coruncanius held this position that Marcus Aurelius held instead of Lucius Verus.

swap.text: Tarquinius Superbus fled to this king of Clusium, whose campaign to reinstall the king was foiled by the determination of Mucius Scaevola.
swap.clue: This figure was saved from death when a would-be assassin mistook his scribe for him, and that assassin thrust his right hand into a fire in an act of defiance against this figure.

question.leadin: Name the following about people who disagreed with the Church.
question.text: This priest of Alexandria put forward the idea that Christ was not coequal with God because God created Christ, giving rise to a namesake heresy addressed by the first Nicene Creed.
question.clue: While speaking at an event, this person was apocryphally slapped by an outraged man from Patara.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the early years of the Byzantine empire.
swap.text: Two advisors to Constantine had this name. The one from Caesarea wrote histories like the Chronicon.
swap.clue: The man who baptized Constantine had this name. A more famous Roman with this name was a Bishop of Caesarea who wrote an Ecclesiastical History of the early church.

question.leadin: This woman was married to Prasutagus, whose will was ignored after he died.
question.text: Name this queen of the Iceni tribe who revolted against her Roman oppressors at Camulodunum, but was eventually defeated by Suetonius Paulinus at Watling Street.
question.clue: This person succeeded Prasutagus as the leader of the Iceni tribe and may have been inspired by to act by her public flogging and the rape of her daughters.

swap.text: Before fleeing to the Balearics, Mago was defeated at this battle near Seville by a concealed force of Romans under Scipio Africanus. The battle of Baecula and this battle ended Carthaginian power in Spain.
swap.clue: This battle's victor unusually placed legions on the wings and auxiliaries in the centre, later creating a concave formation that mirrored a battle occurring ten years prior.

question.text: Alexander the Great's general Eumenes is paired with this rebel leader, who fought one of the earliest guerrilla wars in alliance with the Lusitani. He was betrayed and murdered by his general Perperna.
question.clue: Along with his lieutenant Hirtuleius, he overthrew the governor Quintus Metellus Pius, and then was joined by Marcus Perpenna, though Perpenna eventually had this man murdered at a banquet.

swap.text: The Senate perception of Maximinus's barbarism was partly inspired by his Carpi ancestry from this region. Aurelian abandoned this region whose past leaders, like Decebalus, fought wars against Trajan and Domitian.
swap.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

question.text: Prior to his dictatorship, Cincinnatus was most known in Roman politics for the large fine he had to pay after his son fled a death sentence for physically interfering with holders of this office.
question.answerHtml: tribune of the people [or plebeian tribune; or tribuni plebis]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the agriculture of ancient Rome.
swap.text: This legendary fourth king of Rome, perhaps named for his crooked arm, furthered agricultural development by building the Pons Sublicius across the Tiber. He also built Rome's first prison, the Mamertine, and was succeeded by Tarquinius Priscus.
swap.clue: This fourth king built Rome's first prison and put a wooden bridge across the Tiber.

question.leadin: Name the following people from early Roman history who may or may not have ever really existed, 5-10-20-30.
question.text: At one stage during Porsenna's attack on Rome, this man snuck into his camp to assassinate him but ended up killing the wrong man. When the Etruscans threatened to torture him, he stuck his own hand into a fire and burned it off to save them the trouble.
question.clue: Captured while trying to assassinate the Etruscan king, this man thrust his right hand into a fire in order to demonstrate Roman bravery, scaring the Etruscans into a truce.

swap.text: Recipes for garum and other Roman dishes were contained in this cookbook. This cookbook was published during the reign of Tiberius and its name connotes luxurious food.
swap.clue: In February 2017, Grant Achatz drew on this text to create a project at his Chicago-based establishment Next.
